4. Vocabulary and concept sets

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-04-vocabulary.Rmd
book-04-vocabulary.Rmd

What you will learn

Find meanings, look up names and define a reusable concept set.

This chapter uses the public synthetic GiBleed practice connection from Getting started. You need: the packages and the matching practice connection described in Before you start. Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.4. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

Start this chapter

Start a fresh R session in the book-work directory created in Getting started. Run this setup first:

library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/connection.R")
source("tools/book/practice.R")
practice <- if (book_driver == "DSLite") book_practice("gibleed") else book_connect("gibleed")
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
#> [1] "site"

The site connection is ready. The shared connection.R selects DSLite or Opal and resolves the resource names.

Search a name

A concept ID identifies a meaning. It is not a patient’s ID. Search the GiBleed vocabulary for asthma:

hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Asthma", conns = conns)
knitr::kable(head(hits$pooled[c("concept_name", "domain_id", "vocabulary_id")], 8))
concept_name domain_id vocabulary_id
Childhood asthma Condition SNOMED
Asthma Condition SNOMED
Asthma screening Procedure SNOMED

This is public vocabulary metadata. We show names in tables throughout the book; numeric IDs occur only in code where they specify what to select.

Look up known diagnosis concepts 

answers <- ds.omop.concept.lookup(c(317009L, 80502L), conns = conns)
answers$pooled[c("concept_name", "domain_id")]
#>   concept_name domain_id
#> 1       Asthma Condition
#> 2 Osteoporosis Condition

These are diagnosis meanings. Looking them up does not tell you how many people had either diagnosis.

Include descendants deliberately

A descendant is a more specific meaning below a parent in a vocabulary hierarchy. The asthma hierarchy can include more specific diagnosis concepts.

desc <- ds.omop.concept.descendants(317009L, include_self = FALSE, conns = conns)
knitr::kable(head(desc$pooled["concept_name"], 8))
concept_name
Childhood asthma

Descendants come from concept_ancestor. Check their clinical meaning before including them; a search result is not automatically a study definition.

Store a set 

diagnoses <- omop_concept_set(c(317009L, 80502L))
class(diagnoses)
#> [1] "omop_concept_set" "list"

A concept set is a reusable selection of concepts. For a focused asthma definition, keep a separate named set:

asthma <- omop_concept_set(317009L)
class(asthma)
#> [1] "omop_concept_set" "list"

Both objects are local definitions. Creating one has not selected any patient rows.

Recap

Use IDs to define selections and names to understand them. Chapter 5 switches to a small synthetic questionnaire fixture, where question and answer concepts have different roles.

Try it

Look up inpatient and outpatient visit concepts and show only their names.

Solution

settings <- ds.omop.concept.lookup(c(9201L, 9202L), conns = conns)
settings$pooled["concept_name"]
#>       concept_name
#> 1  Inpatient Visit
#> 2 Outpatient Visit
